plain_english: Then the supreme means of the great lord is praised, the supreme word indeed.
sanskrit_cite: atha paraupayikaṃ praṇigadyate padamanuttarameva maheśituḥ

plain_english: What was declared as mere light, the supreme Bhairava greatness, has only freedom distinguished there.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśamātraṃ yatproktaṃ bhairavīyaṃ paraṃ mahaḥ tatra svatantratāmātramadhikaṃ pravivicyate

plain_english: That light gives light-ness to all; nothing exists apart from it, and the universe appears as being.
sanskrit_cite: yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa sarvasya prakāśatvaṃ prayacchati na ca tadvyatirekyasti viśvaṃ sadvāvabhāsate

plain_english: Therefore that supreme lord, unbarred in his own self-space, reveals the spectacle of creation and destruction.
sanskrit_cite: ato@sau parameśānaḥ svātmavyomanyanargalaḥ iyataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārāḍambarasya pradarśakaḥ

plain_english: As earth, water, and so forth shine unmixed in a pure mirror, so world activities appear in one conscious lord.
sanskrit_cite: nirmale makure yadvadbhānti bhūmijalādayaḥ amiśrāstadvadekasmiṃścinnāthe viśvavṛttayaḥ

plain_english: Similar shining appears in eye, mirror, sky, and water; indeed, in pure form only form appears.
sanskrit_cite: sadṛśaṃ bhāti nayanadarpaṇāmbaravāriṣu tathā hi nirmale rūpe rūpamevāvabhāsate

plain_english: Though the hidden passionate woman touches with her breast-pots the mirror reflecting her beloved beautifully, she is not satisfied.
sanskrit_cite: pracchannarāgiṇī kāntapratibimbitasundaram darpaṇaṃ kucakumbhābhyāṃ spṛśantyapi na tṛpyati

plain_english: Indeed touch of it is not pure; form alone is so, because purity is extreme dense union of same kind.
sanskrit_cite: na hi sparśo@sya vimalo rūpameva tathā yataḥ nairmalyaṃ cātiniviḍasajātīyaikasaṃgatiḥ

plain_english: Purity, as the guru taught, is the seeing capacity of the different arising from non-difference in self, for one who does not abandon self-light.
sanskrit_cite: svasminnabhedādbhinnasya darśanakṣamataiva yā atyaktasvaprakāśasya nairmalyaṃ tadgurūditam

plain_english: Purity is primary for the one consciousness-lord; elsewhere it is partial, by his will.
sanskrit_cite: nairmalyaṃ mukhyamekasya saṃvinnāthasya sarvataḥ aṃśāṃśikātaḥ kvāpyanyadvimalaṃ tattadicchayā

plain_english: For beings, the obstructive body-maya nature belongs to them only; true-knowledge nature is non-obstructive.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvānāṃ yatpratīghāti vapurmāyātmakaṃ hi tat teṣāmevāsti sadvidyāmayaṃ tvapratighātakam

plain_english: Thus revealing an appearance of both forms, the boon-giver shines everywhere by image and reflection view.
sanskrit_cite: tadevamubhayākāramavabhāsaṃ prakāśayan vibhāti varado bimbapratibimbadṛśākhile

plain_english: Someone may argue that rays from the eyes strike a clear surface, bounce back, and thereby grasp one's own face; such a person is now questioned.
sanskrit_cite: yastvāha netratejāṃsi svacchātpratiphalantyalam viparyasya svakaṃ vaktraṃ gṛhṇantīti sa pṛcchyate

plain_english: If the self, presiding over light outside the body, could know by that very light, then what need would there be for a mirror?
sanskrit_cite: dehādanyatra yattejastadadhiṣṭhāturātmanaḥ tenaiva tejasā jñatve ko@rthaḥ syāddarpaṇena tu

plain_english: If the reversed rays became the graspers, the form would be seen on one's own face, not inside the mirror.
sanskrit_cite: viparyastaistu tejobhirgrāhakātmatvamāgataiḥ rūpaṃ dṛśyeta vadane nije na makurāntare

plain_english: If it were really one's own face, that form would appear on one's own face, like touch, as 'mine'; but the mirror image is not tangible and has the nature of being only something seen.
sanskrit_cite: svamukhe sparśavaccaitadrūpaṃ bhāyānmametyalam na tvasya spṛśyabhinnasya vedyaikāntasvarūpiṇaḥ

plain_english: The reflected image is only the shape of visible form; the real thing, joined with touch, smell, taste, and the rest, has those other qualities suppressed in the reflection.
sanskrit_cite: rūpasaṃsthānamātraṃ tatsparśagandharasādibhiḥ nyagbhūtaireva tadyuktaṃ vastu tatpratibimbitam

plain_english: Suppression is due to the absence of graspability, but that does not prove the thing is absent; and that non-graspability arises because there is no real contact with the object and because the image does not actually reside in the mirror.
sanskrit_cite: nyagbhāvo grāhyatābhāvāttadabhāvo@pramāṇataḥ sa cārthasaṃgamābhāvātso@pyādarśe@navasthiteḥ

plain_english: For this reason, properties such as heaviness are not observed in the image; it is not actually situated in the mirror, which serves only as a means for seeing it.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva gurutvādirdharmo naitasya lakṣyate nahyādarśe saṃsthito@sau taddṛṣṭau sa upāyakaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, what appears does not exist there as something separate; the mirror is called its support only conventionally, while lamp, sight, and awareness are, in sequence, the real means of its appearance.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāttu naiṣa bhedena yadbhāti tata ucyate ādhārastatra tūpāyā dīpadṛksaṃvidaḥ kramāt

plain_english: Lamp, eye, and cognition do not produce a separate mirror-like appearance, because they lack hardness and are supremely pure and clear on all sides.
sanskrit_cite: dīpacakṣurvibodhānāṃ kāṭhinyābhāvataḥ param sarvataścāpi nairmalyānna vibhādarśavatpṛthak

plain_english: The God of gods revealed this for the understanding of the deluded: a thing may appear even elsewhere than where it is, yet not fully or truly there.
sanskrit_cite: etacca devadevena darśitaṃ bodhavṛddhaye mūḍhānāṃ vastu bhavati tato@pyanyatra nāpyalam

plain_english: The compassionate teacher explained that the image is not solid, not independent, and not simply stable or unstable; rather, it is the special power of some clear medium.
sanskrit_cite: pratīghāti svatantraṃ no na sthāyyasthāyi cāpi na svacchasyaivaiṣa kasyāpi mahimeti kṛpālunā

plain_english: The teaching on the mirror declared that a reflection has no fixed place, no independent form, no time, no measure, no mutual contact, no removal, and no solidity; it is not simply unreal, nor does it have an essence of its own. By understanding this, delusion is dispelled.
sanskrit_cite: na deśoṃ no rūpaṃ na ca samayayogo na parimā na cānyonyāsaṃgo na ca tadapahānirna ghanatā na cāvastutvaṃ syānna ca kimapi sāraṃ nijamiti dhruvaṃ mohaḥ śāmyediti niradiśaddarpaṇavidhiḥ

plain_english: In the account of reflection presented here, the reflection of sound is what is called an echo.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ pradarśite@mutra pratibimbanavartmani śabdasya pratibimbaṃ yat pratiśrutketi bhaṇyate

plain_english: The echo is not produced by the original sound coming back, because although it is heard as if returning, the speaker does not hear it in that way and distant listeners may not hear the original sound at all.
sanskrit_cite: na cāsau śabdajaḥ śabda āgacchattvena saṃśravāt tenaiva vaktrā dūrasthaiḥ śabdasyāśravaṇādapi

plain_english: Because an echo changes according to the hollows or openings it meets, the reflection of sound behaves like the reflection of a face or other visible form.
sanskrit_cite: piṭhirādipidhānāṃśaviśiṣṭachidrasaṃgatau citratvāccāsya śabdasya pratibimbaṃ mukhādivat

plain_english: Just as a mirror shows the form of another object, an echo is heard as something spoken by another.
sanskrit_cite: idamanyasya vedyasya rūpamityavabhāsate yathādarśe tathā kenāpyuktamākarṇaye tviti

plain_english: Because a reflection must face its original, the perceivers who stand between the source and the reflecting place are the ones who hear the echo.
sanskrit_cite: niyamādbimbasāṃmukhyaṃ pratibimbasya yattataḥ tanmadhyagāḥ pramātāraḥ śṛṇvanti pratiśabdakam

plain_english: A reflection can be perceived even without perceiving the original directly, just as one may see in a mirror the body of a beloved person standing behind oneself.
sanskrit_cite: mukhyagrahaṃ tvapi vinā pratibimbagraho bhavet svapaścātsthaṃ priyaṃ paśyeṭṭaṅkitaṃ mukure vapuḥ

plain_english: Facingness is explained as the reflection's being situated in non-difference from the mirror-like condition in which it appears.
sanskrit_cite: sāṃmukhyaṃ cocyate tādṛgdarpaṇābhedasaṃsthiteḥ

plain_english: Therefore, in the hollow space of a well or jar, the speaker's space is reflected together with sound and appears as if another speaker were there.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ kūpādipiṭhirākāśe tatpratibimbitam vaktrākāśaṃ saśabdaṃ sadbhāti tatparavaktavat

plain_english: Just as someone standing behind a mirror does not directly know the face, someone standing behind such a reflecting space does not directly know the original sound.
sanskrit_cite: yathā cādarśapāścātyabhāgastho vetti no mukham tathā tathāvidhākāśapaścātstho vetti na dhvanim

plain_english: An unmanifest sound is not reflected; its manifestation and hearing occur at the same time, in the second moment.
sanskrit_cite: śabdo na cānabhivyaktaḥ pratibimbati taddhruvam abhivyaktiśrutī tasya samakālaṃ dvitīyake

plain_english: In that moment, the sound's being reflected and its being heard occur at the same time, just as one does not ascertain a hand and its shadow at different times.
sanskrit_cite: kṣaṇe tu pratibimbatvaṃ śrutiśca samakālikā tulyakālaṃ hi no hastatacchāyārūpaniścayaḥ

plain_english: Now that the true nature of reflection has been shown here, we return to the main topic, for reflection properly applies there.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ pradarśite@mutra pratibimbasatattvake prakṛtaṃ brūmahe tatra pratibimbanamarhati

plain_english: Sound is reflected beautifully in space, and touch too can appear as something external, like a blow, pain, or cold, yet it agitates one's own body because it is a reflection.
sanskrit_cite: śabdo nabhasi sānande sparśadhāmani sundaraḥ sparśo@nyo@pi dṛḍhāghātaśūlaśītādikodbhavaḥ parasthaḥ pratibimbatvātsvadehoddhūlanākaraḥ

plain_english: This reflected touch is not the primary one, because it does not reveal an independent chain of effects of its own.
sanskrit_cite: na caiṣa mukhyastatkāryapāramparyāprakāśanāt

plain_english: In the same way, smell appears within the organ of smell, and taste appears clearly in the moisture of the mouth.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ghrāṇāntare gandho raso dantodake sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Just as a reflected form is not seen without the eyes, taste, touch, fragrance, and the rest are not perceived without their proper sense organs, even if they are present.
sanskrit_cite: yathā ca rūpaṃ pratibimbitaṃ dṛśorna cakṣuṣānyena vinā hi lakṣyate tathā rasasparśanasaurabhādikaṃ na lakṣyate@kṣeṇa vinā sthitaṃ tvapi

plain_english: The object of the cognition of an external touch is not located inside the inner field of touch.
sanskrit_cite: na cāntare sparśanadhāmani sthitaṃ bahiḥspṛśonyākṣadhiyaḥ sa gocaraḥ

plain_english: When one's nearby sense organs and inner instruments are properly engaged, the reflection received in the sense organ produces a corresponding activity.
sanskrit_cite: ato@ntikasthasvakatādṛgindriyaprayojanāntaḥkaraṇairyadā kṛtā tadā tadāttaṃ pratibimbamindriye svakāṃ kriyāṃ sūyata eva tādṛśīm

plain_english: An action does not arise from a remembered mental object, because such action truly belongs to the present. Therefore, the excellent touch is situated in that sense organ, having arrived there and being known, and it acts accordingly in the present.
sanskrit_cite: na tu smṛtānmānasagocarādṛtā bhavetkriyā sā kila vartamānataḥ ataḥ sthitaḥ sparśavarastadindriye samāgataḥ sanviditastathākriyaḥ

plain_english: When an external object is impossible, that same excellent touch, reflected within one's own self, produces that pleasurable sensation. It does so within some continuum of subtle channels.
sanskrit_cite: asaṃbhave bāhyagatasya tādṛśaḥ sva eva tasminpratibimbitastathā karoti tāṃ sparśavaraḥ sukhātmikāṃ sa cāpi kasyāmapi nāḍisaṃtatau

plain_english: Therefore, by offering the universe as his own self in the mirror of consciousness, this declares the pure universal nature of the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: tena saṃvittimakure viśvamātmānamarpayat nāthasya vadate@muṣya vimalāṃ viśvarūpatām

plain_english: Just as smell, form, touch, taste, and other qualities, when reflected, shine in a sword by taking on the coloring of that support, like a face and other images reflected there.
sanskrit_cite: yathā ca gandharūpaspṛgrasādyāḥ pratibimbitāḥ tadādhāroparāgeṇa bhānti khaṅge mukhādivat

plain_english: Likewise, this universe, reflected in consciousness, should be understood to rest upon its expansive qualities, such as luminosity and freedom.
sanskrit_cite: tathā viśvamidaṃ bodhe pratibimbitamāśrayet prakāśatvasvatantratvaprabhṛtiṃ dharmavistaram

plain_english: Just as a reflection from all sides may appear in a crystal that is clear on all sides, so too reflections appear in consciousness, which possesses complete clarity.
sanskrit_cite: yathā ca sarvataḥ svacche sphaṭike sarvato bhavet pratibimbaṃ tathā bodhe sarvataḥ svacchatājuṣi

plain_english: Absolute transparency is the non-manifestation of one's own form. Therefore consciousness is the most transparent, unlike a jewel, which grasps and displays its own form.
sanskrit_cite: atyantasvacchatā sā yatsvākṛtyanavabhāsanam ataḥ svacchatamo bodho na ratnaṃ tvākṛtigrahāt

plain_english: A reflection is projected by an external original image, but if everything is a reflection of consciousness itself, what external original image could possibly remain?
sanskrit_cite: pratibimbaṃ ca bimbena bāhyasthena samarpyate tasyaiva pratibimbatve kiṃ bimbamavaśiṣyatām

plain_english: Even if some cause is designated as an external original image, it too becomes a reflection in consciousness; otherwise, outside of consciousness, it would be unreal.
sanskrit_cite: yadvāpi kāraṇaṃ kiṃcidbimbatvenābhiṣicyate tadapi pratibimbatvameti bodhe@nyathā tvasat

plain_english: Thus, protected by the firm weapon of the logic of one's own awareness, the sovereignty of reflection alone expands everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: itthametatsvasaṃvittidṛḍhanyāyāstrarakṣitam sāmrājyameva viśvatra pratibimbasya jṛmbhate

plain_english: An objector asks how a reflection can exist without an original image. The reply is: what can we do, for it is seen? The objector is then challenged to identify that supposed original image.
sanskrit_cite: nanu bimbasya virahe pratibimbaṃ kathaṃ bhavet kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate taddhi nanu tadbimbamucyatām

plain_english: It is not so, because the supposed original lacks the required definition. What is truly called an original image is something unmixed with others, independent, and truly appearing, just like a face.
sanskrit_cite: naivaṃ tallakṣaṇābhāvādbimbaṃ kila kimucyate anyāmiśraṃ svatantraṃ sadbhāsamānaṃ mukhaṃ yathā

plain_english: They define the nature of a reflection as resembling another form without abandoning its own nature, like reflections seen on a sword, a mirror, or a flat surface.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpānapahānena pararūpasadṛkṣatām pratibimbātmatāmāhuḥ khaḍgādarśatalādivat

plain_english: And it is said by the Buddhists that even if external objects exist, cognition is one because it perceives many; it takes on forms resembling many, but it does not itself become many.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ ca sati bāhye@pi dhīrekānekavedanāt anekasadṛśākārā na tvaneketi saugataiḥ

plain_english: But what, then, is the definition of a reflection? It is stated as the impossible manifestation of difference from its substrate due to the unfitness for mixing with another, just as a face appears in a mirror.
sanskrit_cite: nanvitthaṃ pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ taducyate anyavyāmiśraṇāyogāttadbhedāśakyabhāsanam pratibimbamiti prāhurdarpaṇe vadanaṃ yathā

plain_english: This universe, beginning with the supreme reality, is mixed with consciousness and cannot be manifested as different from consciousness; why, then, should it not be called a reflection in consciousness?
sanskrit_cite: bodhamiśramidaṃ bodhādbhedenāśakyabhāsanam paratattvādi bodhe kiṃ pratibimbaṃ na bhaṇyate

plain_english: If this arrangement of the definition is arbitrary, then let the universe be called the original image. Wise people are concerned with reality itself, not with conventional terminology.
sanskrit_cite: lakṣaṇasya vyavasthaiṣākasmāccedbimbamucyatām prājñā vastuni yujyante na tu sāmayike dhvanau

plain_english: But surely a reflection cannot exist without an original image? What of that? In a reflection, the original image does not exist as a separate entity, for it exists only in identity with it.
sanskrit_cite: nanu na pratibimbasya vinā bimbaṃ bhavetsthitiḥ kiṃ tataḥ pratibimbe hi bimbaṃ tādātmyavṛtti na

plain_english: So, even if this stated definition is impossible, there is no loss in taking it as a mere cause; rather, the question comes to rest there.
sanskrit_cite: ataśca lakṣaṇasyāsya proktasya tadasaṃbhave na hānirhetumātre tu praśno@yaṃ paryavasyati

plain_english: Even in the case of what is called an instrumental cause, and not a material one, instrumental causes cannot in any way be possible at any time or place.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi ca nimittākhye nopādāne kathaṃcana nimittakāraṇānāṃ ca kadācitkvāpi saṃbhavaḥ

plain_english: For this very reason, when light is present before one, the form of the beloved may appear vividly transferred there through memory and similar instrumental triggers.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva purovartinyāloke smaraṇādinā nimittena ghanenāstu saṃkrāntadayitākṛtiḥ

plain_english: Otherwise, why would the beloved, who is actually separated, appear as present in consciousness? Consciousness does not go out in front to reach that separation.
sanskrit_cite: anyathā saṃvidārūḍhā kāntā vicchedayoginī kasmādbhāti na vai saṃvid vicchedaṃ purato gatā

plain_english: Therefore, let there be some inner factor called intellect, in which appearances arise clearly by division, as in imagination and in the seeing of dreams.
sanskrit_cite: ata evāntaraṃ kiṃciddhīsaṃjñaṃ bhavatu sphuṭam yatrāsya vicchidā bhānaṃ saṃkalpasvapnadarśane

plain_english: Therefore, let the Lord's powers be the instrumental cause in such cases. Thus this whole universe is a pure reflection in the clear sky of Bhairava-consciousness, not by the grace of anything else.
sanskrit_cite: ato nimittaṃ devasya śaktayaḥ santu tādṛśe itthaṃ viśvamidaṃ nāthe bhairavīyacidambare pratibimbamalaṃ svacche na khalvanyaprasādataḥ

plain_english: That power of the Lord, independent of anything else, by which he is the self of the universe, is declared to be the supreme, unsurpassed goddess Pratibhā.
sanskrit_cite: ananyāpekṣitā yāsya viśvātmatvaṃ prati prabhoḥ tāṃ parāṃ pratibhāṃ devīṃ saṃgirante hyanuttarām

plain_english: Of this Lord Akula, the supreme power is Kaulikī, who shines in the spreading forth of Kula; the Lord is never separated from her.
sanskrit_cite: akulasyāsya devasya kulaprathanaśālinī kaulikī sā parā śaktiraviyukto yayā prabhuḥ

plain_english: The pure united form of those two is remembered as saṃghaṭṭa. That same union is called the power of bliss, because from it the universe is emitted.
sanskrit_cite: tayoryadyāmalaṃ rūpaṃ sa saṃghaṭṭa iti smṛtaḥ ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yato viśvaṃ visṛjyate

plain_english: This goddess is declared to be the principle beyond the supreme and the non-supreme. She is its essence and its heart; that supreme emission is the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: parāparātparaṃ tattvaṃ saiṣā devī nigadyate tatsāraṃ tacca hṛdayaṃ sa visargaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ

plain_english: In the Devīyāmala scripture she is described as Kālakarṣiṇī, and likewise in the Mahāḍāmaraka rite the glorious supreme goddess is placed at the head.
sanskrit_cite: devīyāmalaśāstre sā kathitā kālakarṣiṇī mahāḍāmarake yāge śrīparā mastake tathā

plain_english: In the Śrīpūrva scripture she is described as the true nature of the mothers, as that reflective awareness of being consciousness within this union.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaśāstre sā mātṛsadbhāvatvena varṇitā saṃghaṭṭe@smiṃścidātmatvādyattatpratyavamarśanam

plain_english: The supreme will-power of the fierce powers is the lord; that same power, when agitated in form, becomes the ruler.
sanskrit_cite: icchāśaktiraghorāṇāṃ śaktīnāṃ sā parā prabhuḥ saiva prakṣubdharūpā cedīśitrī saṃprajāyate

plain_english: Then fierce supreme goddesses are born as guides of the shaiva path; self-reflection, formerly the single hero, arises.
sanskrit_cite: tadā ghorāḥ parā devyo jātāḥ śaivādhvadaiśikāḥ svātmapratyavamarśo yaḥ prāgabhūdekavīrakaḥ

plain_english: Established by knowledge-power, this supreme-lower goddess, whose self unfolds the knowable universe, creates the fierce circle of mothers.
sanskrit_cite: jñātavyaviśvonmeṣātmā jñānaśaktitayā sthitaḥ iyaṃ parāparā devī ghorāṃ yā mātṛmaṇḍalīm

plain_english: It continuously creates the lamp of pure and impure paths; when the knowable portion comes with rising agitation from strength.
sanskrit_cite: sṛjatyavirataṃ śuddhāśuddhamārgaikadīpikām jñeyāṃśaḥ pronmiṣankṣobhaṃ yadaiti balavattvataḥ

plain_english: Deficiency-appearance arises in pure consciousness; then the established knowable class is called the beginning of stability.
sanskrit_cite: ūnatābhāsanaṃ saṃvinmātratve jāyate tadā rūḍhaṃ tajjñeyavargasya sthitiprārambha ucyate

plain_english: This establishment is the grasp of varied forms in the ocean of awareness; yogis collect this seed of seed-arrangement.
sanskrit_cite: rūḍhireṣā vibodhābdheścitrākāraparigrahaḥ idaṃ tadbījasaṃdarbhabījaṃ cinvanti yoginaḥ

plain_english: Will-power, said to be two-formed and agitated or unagitated, indeed rests in the self through the duality of objects.
sanskrit_cite: icchāśaktirdvirūpoktā kṣubhitākṣubhitā ca yā iṣyamāṇaṃ hi sā vastudvairūpyeṇātmani śrayet

plain_english: By the quickly shining power of fire-form, desired attainment occurs through stability in the earth-self.
sanskrit_cite: aciradyutibhāsinyā śaktyā jvalanarūpayā iṣyamāṇasamāpattiḥ sthairyeṇātha dharātmanā

plain_english: Although this is knowable in the unfolding power abundantly, nevertheless that is the place of glory, not the eastern birth-place.
sanskrit_cite: unmeṣaśaktāvastyetajjñeyaṃ yadyapi bhūyasā tathāpi vibhavasthānaṃ sā na tu prācyajanmabhūḥ

plain_english: Thus from will-power they say four-formed supreme nectar; because there is no inner agitation, this is not the seed of anyone.
sanskrit_cite: icchāśakterataḥ prāhuścātūrūpyaṃ parāmṛtam kṣobhāntarasyāsadbhāvānnedaṃ bījaṃ ca kasyacit

plain_english: Agitating-nature, seed-nature, support of agitation, and womb-nature are named; the form of consciousness is agitated and also agitates.
sanskrit_cite: prakṣobhakatvaṃ bījatvaṃ kṣobhādhāraśca yonitā kṣobhakaṃ saṃvido rūpaṃ kṣubhyati kṣobhayatyapi

plain_english: Agitation would be the knowable quality; agitating is its exclusion, while the inner undivided one-seed desire to emit remains.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhaḥ syājjñeyadharmatvaṃ kṣobhaṇā tadbahiṣkṛtiḥ antaḥsthaviśvābhinnaikabījāṃśavisisṛkṣutā

plain_english: Agitation in that will is the appearance of truth-will; they know agitating, and having attained unity, that will becomes effective.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobho@tadicche tattvecchābhāsanaṃ kṣobhaṇāṃ viduḥ yadaikyāpattimāsādya tadicchā kṛtinī bhavet

plain_english: The sons of Shri Somananda call this support of agitation the undifferentiated distinctness of the beginnings of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhādhāramimaṃ prāhuḥ śrīsomānandaputrakāḥ saṃvidāmīṣaṇādīnāmanudbhinnaviśeṣakam

plain_english: Whatever is only knowable is that seed; by union, seedness is in sound; that same seed's desire to emit is the origin from which this grasped shining different form of consciousness-self arises.
sanskrit_cite: yajjñeyamātraṃ tadbījaṃ yadyogādbījatā svare tasya bījasya saivoktā visisṛkṣā ya udbhavaḥ yato grāhyamidaṃ bhāsyadbhinnakalpaṃ cidātmanaḥ

plain_english: This is agitation; agitating, however, expels the silent other-mother-going and the sudden indifference-part from consciousness by force.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa kṣobhaḥ kṣobhaṇā tu tūṣṇīṃbhūtānyamātṛgam haṭhādyadaudāsīnyāṃśacyāvanaṃ saṃvido balāt

plain_english: Although born, that desire to emit becomes accomplished from the unity of other reflection; thus the support of agitation is proclaimed.
sanskrit_cite: jātāpi visisṛkṣāsau yadvimarśāntaraikyataḥ kṛtārthā jāyate kṣobhādhāro@traitatprakīrtitam

plain_english: Then that knowable interval desires a different form from the universe-seed; all external reflection will manifest.
sanskrit_cite: tatastadāntaraṃ jñeyaṃ bhinnakalpatvamicchati viśvabījādataḥ sarva bāhyaṃ bimbaṃ vivartsyati

plain_english: The true nature of the agitated-agitating state has been shown by me, as spoken by Shri Maheshvara, by the grace of the guru.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhyakṣobhakabhāvasya satattvaṃ darśitaṃ mayā śrīmanmaheśvareṇoktaṃ guruṇā yatprasādataḥ

plain_english: We speak of the subject; this is not seed, the four letters, nor does it attain the status of support of agitation.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtaṃ brūmahe nedaṃ bījaṃ varṇacatuṣṭayam nāpi yoniryato naitatkṣobhādhāratvamṛcchati

plain_english: In the self only, by rest, that spoken immortal nature; thus the previously spoken fivefold is mutual.
sanskrit_cite: ātmanyeva ca viśrāntyā tatproktamamṛtātmakam itthaṃ prāguditaṃ yattatpañcakaṃ tatparasparam

plain_english: From the mutual mixing of rising varied forms, the supreme higher vibration and bliss rise together.
sanskrit_cite: ucchaladvividhākāramanyonyavyatimiśraṇāt yo@nuttaraḥ paraḥ spando yaścānandaḥ samucchalan

plain_english: From that collision of will-unfolding going to great variety, supreme bliss-consciousness is in will-power when employed.
sanskrit_cite: tāvicchonmeṣasaṃghaṭṭādgacchato@tivicitratām anuttarānandacitī icchāśaktau niyojite

plain_english: Thus the triangle is called beautiful emission-bliss; supreme bliss-powers attain establishment there.
sanskrit_cite: trikoṇamiti tatprāhurvisargāmodasundaram anuttarānandaśaktī tatra rūḍhimupāgate

plain_english: When two triangles join, the configuration moves into a six-spoked state; yet even in that unfolding, it goes again into absorption in that same reality.
sanskrit_cite: trikoṇadvitvayogena vrajataḥ ṣaḍarasthitim ta evonmeṣayoge@pi punastanmayatāṃ gate

plain_english: The stirring that arises in the unfolding of will, mutually interacting, clearly manifests the form of the power of action; this is also said of that movement.
sanskrit_cite: kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ rūpamabhivyaṅktaḥ parasparam icchonmeṣagataḥ kṣobho yaḥ proktastadgaterapi

plain_english: Those two powers indeed share that same form and do not stand otherwise. But how can unsurpassedness and bliss, which by their own nature are free from division, appear in this way?
sanskrit_cite: te eva śaktī tādrūpyabhāginyau nānyathāsthite nanvanuttaratānandau svātmanā bhedavarjitau

plain_english: How can those two, free from division, take on such variegation within their own self? Listen: this Lord of consciousness is by nature unlimited.
sanskrit_cite: kathametāvatīmenāṃ vaicitrīṃ svātmani śritau śṛṇu tāvadayaṃ saṃvinnātho@parimitātmakaḥ

plain_english: If the great Lord, master of the dissolution and arising of endless varieties of power, were to remain in only one form, then what would follow?
sanskrit_cite: anantaśaktivaicitryalayodayakaleśvaraḥ asthāsyadekarūpeṇa vapuṣā cenmaheśvaraḥ

plain_english: He would abandon his great-lordship and his nature as consciousness, like a pot or any other finite thing. For limited luminosity is indeed the defining mark of the inert.
sanskrit_cite: maheśvaratvaṃ saṃvittvaṃ tadatyakṣyaddhaṭādivat paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam

plain_english: Awareness is distinct from the inert because it cannot be measured. Therefore, his own powers surge up like waves in the great ocean of awareness.
sanskrit_cite: jaḍādvilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate tena bodhamahasindhorullāsinyaḥ svaśaktayaḥ

plain_english: Like waves, they take on the variegation of their own self-union. That mutual diversity of the powers is the diversity of their own inner union.
sanskrit_cite: āśrayantyūrmaya iva svātmasaṃghaṭṭacitratām svātmasaṃghaṭṭavaicitryaṃ śaktīnāṃ yatparasparam

plain_english: They declare this very diversity to be the supreme, clear body of the power of action, in that fourteenth abode where the three powers have become manifest.
sanskrit_cite: etadeva paraṃ prāhuḥ kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ vapuḥ asmiṃścaturdaśe dhāmni sphuṭībhūtatriśaktike

plain_english: Therefore the Teacher declared this to be the trident in the Śrīpūrva teaching, and teachers who see reality have also called it stainless.
sanskrit_cite: triśūlatvamataḥ prāha śāstā śrīpūrvaśāsane nirañjanamidaṃ coktaṃ gurubhistattvadarśibhiḥ

plain_english: The power-holder seems affected because will, knowledge, and action appear separately; yet power itself is never affected by anything.
sanskrit_cite: śaktimānañjyate yasmānna śaktirjātu kenacit icchā jñānaṃ kriyā ceti yatpṛthakpṛthagañjyate

plain_english: That same triad, through the power-holder's own modes such as willing and the rest, appears clearly; but when it shines forth in unity, then it does so as one.
sanskrit_cite: tadeva śaktimatsvaiḥ svairiṣyamāṇādikaiḥ sphuṭam etattritayamaikyena yadā tu prasphurettadā

plain_english: Because the three powers cannot be grasped by any one-sided condition and mutually resist such limitation, they become a single vibrant trident. The yogi who quickly becomes absorbed in that trident becomes stainless.
sanskrit_cite: na kenacidupādheyaṃ svasvavipratiṣedhataḥ lolībhūtamataḥ śaktitritayaṃ tattriśūlakam yasminnāśu samāveśādbhavedyogī nirañjanaḥ

plain_english: In this way, the octad that begins from the supreme nectar state, when divided through Brahmi and the other forms, clearly expands into eight octads.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ parāmṛtapadādārabhyāṣṭakamīdṛśam brāhmyādirūpasaṃbhedādyātyaṣṭāṣṭakatāṃ sphuṭam

plain_english: Here the supreme power, even while making her own body manifest, takes the form of bindu because of the stain associated with the knowable aspect.
sanskrit_cite: atrānuttaraśaktiḥ sā svaṃ vapuḥ prakaṭasthitam kurvantyapi jñeyakalākāluṣyādvindurūpiṇī

plain_english: When the power of action has arisen in the abode of moon, sun, and fire, the undivided light that is present there is, for us, the supreme bindu.
sanskrit_cite: uditāyāṃ kriyāśaktau somasūryāgnidhāmani avibhāgaḥ prakāśo yaḥ sa binduḥ paramo hi naḥ

plain_english: And in the teaching on the protection of the principles, the supreme Lord said that the bindu stands within the circle of the heart-lotus and has a nature consisting of the human, power, and Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: tattvarakṣāvidhāne ca taduktaṃ parameśinā hṛtpadmamaṇḍalāntaḥstho naraśaktiśivātmakaḥ

plain_english: The bindu should be understood, through the distinction of dissolution, as pure and delivering. It is that sound whose nature is nada and which is present in all beings.
sanskrit_cite: boddhavyo layabhedena vindurvimalatārakaḥ yo@sau nādātmakaḥ śabdaḥ sarvaprāṇiṣvavasthitaḥ

plain_english: Though described by divisions of below and above, it remains without activity. Whatever variety appears, such as soothing or sharp qualities and white or red colors, belongs to that apparent diversity.
sanskrit_cite: adha+ūrdhvavibhāgena niṣkriyeṇāvatiṣṭhate hlādataikṣṇyādi vaicitryaṃ sitaraktādikaṃ ca yat

plain_english: That light is in itself independent of those variations, as the teacher said. Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor even fire illuminates it.
sanskrit_cite: svayaṃ tannirapekṣo@sau prakāśo gururāha ca yanna sūryo na vā somo nāgnirbhāsayate@pi ca

plain_english: Sun, moon, and fire have no splendor of their own apart from that light. Rather, it is consciousness that shines in this way.
sanskrit_cite: na cārkasomavahnīnāṃ tatprakāśādvinā mahaḥ kimapyasti nijaṃ kiṃ tu saṃviditthaṃ prakāśate

plain_english: Joined with varied conditions that arise from its own freedom, the one light takes on an inner variety, such as sharpness and other qualities.
sanskrit_cite: svasvātantryaprabhāvodyadvicitropādhisaṃgataḥ prakāśo yāti taikṣṇyādimavāntaravicitratām

plain_english: Even the sun, which is hard to look at, becomes delightful to the eyes when its light falls on water. See how powerful a conditioning medium can be.
sanskrit_cite: durdarśano@pi gharmāṃśuḥ patitaḥ pāthasāṃ pathi netrānandatvamabhyeti paśyopādheḥ prabhāvitām

plain_english: The light seen in the sun and other things is stained by limiting conditions, and therefore it depends on the Maheshvara light, the light of consciousness itself.
sanskrit_cite: sūryādiṣu prakāśo@sāvupādhikaluṣīkṛtaḥ saṃvitprakāśaṃ māheśamata eva hyapekṣate

plain_english: Clearly manifest mere light is called the sun. That aspect which pours forth the essential content of what is to be illuminated is called the moon.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśamātraṃ suvyaktaṃ sūrya ityucyate sphuṭam prakāśyavastusārāṃśavarṣi tatsoma ucyate

plain_english: They call the sun the means of knowing and the moon the object to be known. Though never separated from each other, the two also stand as independent.
sanskrit_cite: sūrya pramāṇamityāhuḥ somaṃ meyaṃ pracakṣate anyonyamaviyuktau tau svatantrāvapyubhau sthitau

plain_english: When this pair, as enjoyer and enjoyed, turns toward each other, there arises a blazing form of consciousness that is proclaimed as fire.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktṛbhogyobhayātmaitadanyonyonmukhatāṃ gatam tato jvalanacidrūpaṃ citrabhānuḥ prakīrtitaḥ

plain_english: The supreme principle of fire is nothing other than the knower's own reality. It is consciousness itself, not dependent on anything else because it is identical with what is to be known.
sanskrit_cite: yo@yaṃ vahneḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ pramāturidameva tat saṃvideva tu vijñeyatādātmyādanapekṣiṇī

plain_english: Because of its freedom, consciousness is called the knower. It appears varied through differences among knowables, expanded by the diverse appearances of objects that arise on the moon side and are taken up by the fire aspect.
sanskrit_cite: svatantratvātpramātoktā vicitro jñeyabhedataḥ somāṃśadāhyavastūtthavaicitryābhāsabṛṃhitaḥ

plain_english: For this reason the great Lord called this fire Citrabhanu. The status of consciousness is entirely independent of the whole set of means that begin with the knowable.
sanskrit_cite: tata evāgniruditaścitrabhānurmaheśinā jñeyādyupāyasaṃghātanirapekṣaiva saṃvidaḥ

plain_english: Consciousness stands as the immediate sense, 'I am the knower.' But one who knows like a person who merely knows scripture is not truly knowing in essence, because that knowledge depends on experienced objects rather than on its own self-form.
sanskrit_cite: sthitirmātāhamasmīti jñātā śāstrajñavadyataḥ ajña eva yato jñātānubhavātmā na rūpataḥ

plain_english: That is not true knowership which depends on a pure knowable or anything similar. In such a state, the term knowership is used only in a secondary sense, because of a certain fitness.
sanskrit_cite: na tu sā jñātṛtā yasyāṃ śuddhajñeyādyapekṣate tasyāṃ daśāyāṃ jñātṛtvamucyate yogyatāvaśāt

plain_english: That dependent knowing is only a kind of measuring, constructed by the limited knower. Consciousness, even when it surges forth, is not divided by temporal sequence.
sanskrit_cite: mānataiva tu sā prācyapramātṛparikalpitā ucchalantyapi saṃvittiḥ kālakramavivarjanāt

plain_english: As soon as consciousness arises, it is already full and contains within itself the knower, the known, and the rest. Ordinary actions like cooking, by contrast, unfold in sequence because they are limited by time.
sanskrit_cite: uditaiva satī pūrṇā mātṛmeyādirūpiṇī pākādistu kriyā kālaparicchedātkramocitā

plain_english: Even if one thinks of an action as ending in a final moment, that alone does not make it the completed act of cooking. In this way, the principle of light is established as having the nature of moon, sun, and fire.
sanskrit_cite: matāntyakṣaṇavandhyāpi na pākatvaṃ prapadyate itthaṃ prakāśatattvasya somasūryāgnitā sthitā

plain_english: Even so, the primary nature of these three is not removed: they remain mere light. Of these, the first, short form is called the sun.
sanskrit_cite: api mukhyaṃ tatprakāśamātratvaṃ na vyapohyate eṣāṃ yatprathamaṃ rūpaṃ hrasvaṃ tatsūrya ucyate

plain_english: Because of long rest arising from stirring and bliss, it is called Soma. That supreme state, named Pluta, is established beyond the bliss of Soma.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhānandavaśāddīrghaviśrāntyā soma ucyate yattatparaṃ plutaṃ nāma somānandātparaṃ sthitam

plain_english: Those skilled in scripture call that light-natured state fiery. Here, when the three abodes are established, what remains is mere light.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśarūpaṃ tatprāhurāgneyaṃ śāstrakovidāḥ atra prakāśamātraṃ yatsthite dhāmatraye sati

plain_english: In scripture this is spoken of as the bindu and is regarded as the Shiva-bindu. It is indeed other than the letter ma, bearing only its shadow.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ vindutayā śāstre śivavindurasau mataḥ makārādanya evāyaṃ tacchāyāmātradhṛdyathā

plain_english: Ra, la, and ha become established in the forms of ṣa, ṇ, ṭha, and visarga, just as the vowel i becomes another vowel through the shadow of a part of ra.
sanskrit_cite: ralahāḥ ṣaṇṭhavaisargavarṇarūpatvasaṃsthitāḥ ikāra eva rephāṃśacchāyayānyo yathā svaraḥ

plain_english: In the same way, from the great Lord arises another principle. Even while appearing as a vowel in two ways, that inner desire to emit within him is declared to be the supreme Kauliki power.
sanskrit_cite: tathaiva mahaleśādaḥ so@nyo dvedhāsvaro@pi san asyāntarvisisṛkṣāsau yā proktā kaulikī parā

plain_english: That very same power, through the force of stirring, certainly becomes visarga. This is said in the Trishiras scripture in the discussion that concludes with the pervasion of kala.
sanskrit_cite: saiva kṣobhavaśādeti visargātmakatāṃ dhruvam uktaṃ ca triśiraḥśāstre kalāvyāptyantacarcane

plain_english: The seventeenth kala, therefore having the form of nectar, spreads forth through the movement of the bindu of its own higher and lower nature.
sanskrit_cite: kalā saptadaśī tasmādamṛtākārarūpiṇī parāparasvasvarūpabindugatyā visarpitā

plain_english: When devoid of visarga, that power which illuminates all things is called Shakti-Kundalini, and likewise Prana-Kundalini.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśyaṃ sarvavastūnāṃ visargarahitā tu sā śaktikuṇḍalikā caiva prāṇakuṇḍalikā tathā

plain_english: But at the terminal point of visarga it is called supreme Kundalini, and also the space of Shiva; it is called the supreme abode of the self of Brahman.
sanskrit_cite: visargaprāntadeśe tu parā kuṇḍalinīti ca śivavyometi paramaṃ brahmātmasthānamucyate

plain_english: Mere visarga is the Lord's play of creation and dissolution: it is the casting of his own self into his own self, the state belonging to visarga.
sanskrit_cite: visargamātraṃ nāthasya sṛṣṭisaṃhāravibhramāḥ svātmanaḥ svātmani svātmakṣepo vaisargikī sthitiḥ

plain_english: Visarga, thus emitted and having reached a contracted state, is defined as Hamsa, as breath, as a consonant, and as a stop consonant.
sanskrit_cite: visarga evamutsṛṣṭa āśyānatvamupāgataḥ haṃsaḥ prāṇo vyañjanaṃ ca sparśaśca paribhāṣyate

plain_english: That unsurpassed supreme abode is called Akula. The visarga of that Lord is called the Kauliki power.
sanskrit_cite: anuttaraṃ paraṃ dhāma tadevākulamucyate visargastasya nāthasya kaulikī śaktirucyate

plain_english: That very same state of visarga, when bliss rises in sequence, becomes a surging forth that extends to clearly manifest action-power.
sanskrit_cite: visargatā ca saivāsyā yadānandodayakramāt spaṣṭībhūtakriyāśaktiparyantā procchalatsthitiḥ

plain_english: Visarga indeed, having drawn in so much otherness within itself, is like the ocean in this form: an endless succession of waves.
sanskrit_cite: visarga eva tāvānyadākṣiptaitāvadātmakaḥ iyadrūpaṃ sāgarasya yadanantormisaṃtatiḥ

plain_english: Therefore this visarga, consisting of the unmanifest ha and ka, is called the principle of Kama in the revered Kula cave.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva visargo@yamavyaktahakalātmakaḥ kāmatattvamiti śrīmatkulaguhvara ucyate

plain_english: That imperishable unmanifest, situated in the throat of the beloved, is of the nature of sound, without desire, and free from meditation and concentration.
sanskrit_cite: yattadakṣaramavyakta kāntākaṇṭhe vyavasthitam dhvanirūpamanicchaṃ tu dhyānadhāraṇavarjitam

plain_english: Having fixed the mind there, one should subdue the world all at once. Therefore, just as visarga abides clearly in Hamsa, so too is its state understood.
sanskrit_cite: tatra cittaṃ samādhāya vaśayedyugapajjagat ata eva visargasya haṃse yadvatsphuṭā sthitiḥ

plain_english: In the same way, those beginning with Anuttara abide as the range from ka to sa. From Anuttara comes the clear emanation of the fivefold ka-group.
sanskrit_cite: tadvatsānuttarādīnāṃ kādisāntatayā sthitiḥ anuttarātkavargasya sūtiḥ pañcātmanaḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: Because it is necessarily of the nature of the five powers, this is clear in each case, as the power of will, abiding in its own nature, appears from a single form.
sanskrit_cite: pañcaśaktyātmatovaśa ekaikatra yathā sphuṭaḥ icchāśakteḥ svasvarūpasaṃsthāyā ekarūpataḥ

plain_english: The ca-group is of the nature of the five powers and consists of gradual clear manifestation. Then, through connection with a brief activity that shares in the stain of the knowable, the next stage arises.
sanskrit_cite: cavargaḥ pañcaśaktyātmā kramaprasphuṭatātmakaḥ yā tūktā jñeyakāluṣyabhākkṣipracarayogataḥ

plain_english: From that twofold power are born the pair of groups beginning with ṭa and ta. But from unfolding comes the pa-group, because through it the universe is completed.
sanskrit_cite: dvirūpāyāstato jātaṃ ṭa-tādyaṃ vargayugmakam unmeṣātpādivargastu yato viśvaṃ samāpyate

plain_english: This, having the form of the knowable and extending up to the twenty-fifth, is clearly manifest. Because it is knowable and thus clear, this much is declared to have the form of the stop consonants.
sanskrit_cite: jñeyarūpamidaṃ pañcaviṃśatyantaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam jñeyatvātsphuṭataḥ proktametāvatsparśarūpakam

plain_english: And the power of will, which is twofold as stirred and unstirred, turns toward a portion of a different power and goes to the state of ya.
sanskrit_cite: icchāśaktiśca yā dvedhā kṣubhitākṣubhitatvataḥ sā vijātīyaśaktyaṃśapronmukhī yāti yātmatām

plain_english: That very same power, more quickly tinged by the stain of the knowable, and turned toward what is different, goes to the state of ra and to the state of la.
sanskrit_cite: saiva śīghrataropāttajñeyakāluṣyarūṣitā vijātīyonmukhatvena ratvaṃ latvaṃ ca gacchati

plain_english: In the same way, the twofold unfolding power, when it moves toward the power of otherness, becomes the letter va, which pours forth the essence of creation.
sanskrit_cite: tadvadunmeṣaśaktirdvirūpā vaijātyaśaktigā vakāratvaṃ prapadyeta sṛṣṭisārapravarṣakam

plain_english: Will itself, having reached supreme bliss, is called air when joined with swiftness; through shining it becomes fire, and through firmness it becomes earth.
sanskrit_cite: icchaivānuttarānandayātā śīghratvayogataḥ vāyurityucyate vahnirbhāsanātsthairyato dharā

plain_english: This group of four is said to be inner because it is contained within will and the other powers and abides in its own completion.
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ catuṣkamantaḥsthamata eva nigadyate icchādyantargatatvena svasamāptau ca saṃsthiteḥ

plain_english: The joining of the same-kind powers, beginning with will, is said to be a form of agitation, and this also applies to those whose nature involves both agitation and nonagitation.
sanskrit_cite: sajātīyakaśaktīnāmicchādyānāṃ ca yojanam kṣobhātmakamidaṃ prāhuḥ kṣobhākṣobhātmanāmapi

plain_english: When the supreme meets its own sameness, a twofold movement arises. One of these remains simply the supreme and can give rise to bliss.
sanskrit_cite: anuttarasya sājātye bhavettu dvitayī gatiḥ anuttaraṃ yattatraikaṃ taccedānandasūtaye

plain_english: In that joining, a clearly agitated union arises. Even here the supreme abode is present, and the second aspect also serves the purpose of bringing something forth.
sanskrit_cite: prabhaviṣyati tadyoge yogaḥ kṣobhātmakaḥ sphuṭaḥ atrāpyanuttaraṃ dhāma dvitīyamapi sūtaye

plain_english: Without agitation, the supreme nature is not sufficient. Will may lack action, or it may be tinged by what is to be willed.
sanskrit_cite: na paryāptaṃ tadā kṣobhaṃ vinaivānuttarātmatā icchā yā karmaṇā hīnā yā caiṣṭavyena rūṣitā

plain_english: Divided by swiftness and firmness, will becomes threefold, appearing as unopened, opening, and fully opened.

sanskrit_cite: tathāhi tatragā yāsāvicchāśaktirudīritā saiva sūte svakartavyamantaḥsthaṃ sveṣṭarūpakam

sanskrit_cite: kādi-hāntamidaṃ prahuḥ kṣobhādhāratayā budhāḥ yonirūpeṇa tasyāpi yoge kṣobhāntaraṃ vrajet

plain_english: Through that indication, the fiftieth phoneme arises, well established as before in the level known as the twenty-fifth.

plain_english: There are two tetrads, in sequence, moving in difference and non-difference; the first tetrad is skilled in joining together the divisions of consciousness.

plain_english: A consonant becomes manifest through articulation, but its life-breath is the vowel; indeed, in the whole stream of phonemes, the root is only the group of six vowels.
sanskrit_cite: vyaktiyogādvyañjanaṃ tatsvaraprāṇaṃ yataḥ kila svarāṇāṃ ṣaṭkameveha mūlaṃ syādvarṇasaṃtatau

plain_english: Those six deities are the principal rays of the sun, and within those very solar rays there is a lunar digit.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍdevatāstu tā eva ye mukhyāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ saurāṇāmeva raśmīnāmantaścāndrakalā yataḥ

plain_english: Therefore the triad of long vowels is clearly a lunar body; and the moon is nothing other than the enjoyable and the enjoyer—there is no third thing apart from them.
sanskrit_cite: ato@tra dīrghatritayaṃ sphuṭaṃ cāndramasaṃ vapuḥ candraśca nāma naivānyo bhogyaṃ bhoktuśca nāparam

plain_english: The enjoyer alone becomes established as twofold by appearing as the enjoyable; for a pot does not have enjoyability as its own nature—rather, that belongs to the subject.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktaiva bhogyabhāvena dvaividhyātsaṃvyavasthitaḥ ghaṭasya na hi bhogyatvaṃ svaṃ vapurmātṛgaṃ hi tat

plain_english: Therefore, the establishment that occurs in the subject is called the object's enjoyability; the unsurpassed appears through the states of being the object of awareness and the subject of awareness.
sanskrit_cite: ato mātari yā rūḍhiḥ sāsya bhogyatvamucyate anuttaraṃ parāmṛśyaparāmarśakabhāvataḥ

plain_english: The enjoyable—will and the rest—attains the form of a collision; likewise, when will and the other powers rest on the ground of unsurpassed bliss, they become enjoyable.

plain_english: The arising of the juncture phonemes is said to be the form of the enjoyer, and the god who is made of unsurpassed bliss is said to be the enjoyer alone.
sanskrit_cite: saṃdhyakṣarāṇāmudayo bhoktṛrūpaṃ ca kathyate anuttarānandamayo devo bhoktaiva kathyate

plain_english: Will and the rest are only the enjoyable, and for that reason they are his powers; if the enjoyable dissolves into the enjoyer, then the enjoyer becomes clearly manifest in his true reality.
sanskrit_cite: icchādikaṃ bhogyameva tata evāsya śaktitā bhogyaṃ bhoktari līnaṃ ced bhoktā tadvastutaḥ sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Therefore the triad, essence of six, of consciousness-will-opening nature, that same threefold, they call Bhairava's supreme greatness.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ trikaṃ sāraṃ cidiṣyunmeṣaṇātmakam tadeva tritayaṃ prāhurbhairavasya paraṃ mahaḥ

plain_english: That triad of the supreme lord is the full power sung; by it the universe is drawn, because in this worshipped.
sanskrit_cite: tattrikaṃ parameśasya pūrṇā śaktiḥ pragīyate tenākṣiptaṃ yato viśvamato@sminsamupāsite

plain_english: Worship born in a cut and barren universe-power: thus this greatness is only so much, and that much is not possible.
sanskrit_cite: viśvaśaktāvavacchedavandhye jātamupāsanam ityeṣa mahimaitāvāniti tāvanna śakyate

plain_english: Who would make a limit to the power of the unlimited? Therefore the god is supreme by freedom and supremacy.
sanskrit_cite: aparicchinnaśakteḥ kaḥ kuryācchaktiparicchidām tasmādanuttaro devaḥ svācchandyānuttaratvataḥ

plain_english: Endowed with emanation power, completed as universe-formed; thus the great lord has fifty-reflection full power.
sanskrit_cite: visargaśaktiyuktatvātsaṃpanno viśvarūpakaḥ evaṃ pañcāśadāmarśapūrṇaśaktirmaheśvaraḥ

plain_english: Reflection-self is one; indeed other powers are established in this only; the eighty-one-footed goddess will be included here.
sanskrit_cite: vimarśātmaika evānyāḥ śaktayo@traiva niṣṭhitāḥ ekāśītipadā devī hyatrāntarbhāvayiṣyate

plain_english: In one reflection nature, sound-mass is Bhairava; by reflection-shadow and union, that same power is mother-power.
sanskrit_cite: ekāmarśasvabhāvatve śabdarāśiḥ sa bhairavaḥ āmṛśyacchāyayā yogātsaiva śaktiśca mātṛkā

plain_english: She is different in womb from sound-mass collision; Malini is as before ninefold reflection, having separate class nature.

plain_english: In each reflection ascent, that same is fifty-natured; thus by sound penetration, supreme reflection is natured.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikāmarśarūḍhau tu saiva pañcāśadātmikā itthaṃ nādānuvedhena parāmarśasvabhāvakaḥ

plain_english: Shiva, as mother and father, maker, is established everywhere; emanation indeed is power; this again is as Shiva-bindu.
sanskrit_cite: śivo mātāpitṛtvena kartā viśvatra saṃsthitaḥ visarga eva śākto@yaṃ śivabindutayā punaḥ

plain_english: Womb-made infinite universe, he resorts to supreme selfhood in unlimited universe inner essence, in own self of the lord.
sanskrit_cite: garbhīkṛtānantaviśvaḥ śrayate@nuttarātmatām aparicchinnaviśvāntaḥsāre svātmani yaḥ prabhoḥ

plain_english: Supreme reflection is called I by fullness of the lord; supreme first emanation ending is power-natured.

plain_english: In withdrawn all-universe supreme, she dissolves; that universe stands within power, she supreme in supreme.

plain_english: That her thus, what is true, by the lord enclosure-making; by that, in Trishika treatise, power's enclosed form.
sanskrit_cite: tattasyāmiti yatsatyaṃ vibhunā saṃpuṭīkṛtiḥ tena śrītrīśikāśāstre śakteḥ saṃpuṭitākṛtiḥ

plain_english: In consciousness shines which universe; there also indeed by consciousness; that triad has gone to compaction by pair union.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvittau bhāti yadviśvaṃ tatrāpi khalu saṃvidā tadetattritayaṃ dvandvayogātsaṃghātatāṃ gatam

plain_english: One only supreme form of Bhairava is I-self-natured; emanation power of Shambhu thus exists everywhere.

plain_english: From that indeed all this bliss essence agitation; for thus in sweet song, touch, or sandalwood etc.
sanskrit_cite: tata evasamasto@yamānandarasavibhramaḥ tathāhi madhure gīte sparśe vā candanādike

plain_english: In mediacy disappearance, which throbbing in heart is bliss power; that same called, because heartful person.
sanskrit_cite: mādhyasthyavigame yāsau hṛdaye spandamānatā ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yataḥ sahṛdayo janaḥ

plain_english: First, having abandoned all duty in void fire, mind-rest named, then after that.
sanskrit_cite: pūrva visṛjyasakalaṃ kartavyaṃ śūnyatānale cittaviśrāntisaṃjño@yamāṇavastadanantaram

plain_english: Toward seen, heard, etc. things in own consciousness, mind awakening called, Shakti-joy fullness natured.
sanskrit_cite: dṛṣṭaśrutāditadvastupronmukhatvaṃ svasaṃvidi cittasaṃbodhanāmoktaḥ śāktollāsabharātmakaḥ

plain_english: As before future towardness possible limited dissolution from, mind dissolution named this, emanation Shambhava supreme.

sanskrit_cite: tattvarakṣāvidhāne@to visargatraidhamucyate hṛtpadmakośamadhyasthastayoḥ saṃghaṭṭa iṣyate

sanskrit_cite: visargo@ntaḥ sa ca proktaścittaviśrāntilakṣaṇaḥ dvitīyaḥ sa visargastu cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ

plain_english: When this moving and unmoving world becomes one, it shines here; indeed, some difference between object and subject is expected here.
sanskrit_cite: ekībhūtaṃ vibhātyatra jagadetaccarācaram grāhyagrāhakabhedo vai kiṃcidatreṣyate yadā

plain_english: Then that [reality] is called whole, yet partless through Śiva-yoga, being of the nature of a complete grasping that interrupts object and subject.
sanskrit_cite: tadāsau sakalaḥ prokto niṣkalaḥ śivayogataḥ grāhyagrāhakavicchittisaṃpūrṇagrahaṇātmakaḥ

plain_english: The third is indeed that visarga: subtle, of unity-being nature, marked by the dissolution of mind, the consciousness-self completed in itself.
sanskrit_cite: tṛtīyaḥ sa visargastu cittapralayalakṣaṇaḥ ekībhāvātmakaḥ sūkṣmo vijñānātmātmanirvṛtaḥ

plain_english: In the doctrine of Śrī Siddhayogīśvarī, the ascertained meaning is this: here Kuṇḍalinī is the seed, a living being of conscious nature.
sanskrit_cite: nirūpito@yamarthaḥ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate sātra kuṇḍalinī bījaṃ jīvabhūtā cidātmikā

plain_english: The triad born from that, called the unfolding of steady desire; then letters again; the phase extends from the letter a up to vaisargikī.
sanskrit_cite: tajjaṃ dhruvecchonmeṣākhyaṃ trikaṃ varṇāstataḥ punaḥ ā ityavarṇādityādiyāvadvaisargikī kalā

plain_english: The phonemes from ka to sa, together with the fivefold visarga, are both outside and inside, in the heart, in sound, and in the supreme state.
sanskrit_cite: kakārādisakārāntā visargātpañcadhā sa ca bahiścāntaśca hṛdaye nāde@tha parame pade

plain_english: The bindu in the self pervades from the heart to the head; indeed, mantras lacking first and last would be like an autumn cloud.
sanskrit_cite: bindurātmani mūrdhāntaṃ hṛdayādvyāpako hi saḥ ādimāntyavihīnāstu mantrāḥ syuḥ śaradabhravat

sanskrit_cite: gurorlakṣaṇametāvadādimāntyaṃ ca vedayet pūjyaḥ so@hamiva jñānī bhairavo devatātmakaḥ

plain_english: Whatever verse, gāthā, or the like is joined with beginning and end, therefore, knowing thus, one sees all as mantra indeed.
sanskrit_cite: ślokagāthādi yatkiṃcidādimāntyayutaṃ tataḥ tasmādvidaṃstathā sarvaṃ mantratvenaiva paśyati

plain_english: In the Vedanta called Aitareya, the Supreme Lord has ascertained in detail that the visarga-power of the universe is its cause.
sanskrit_cite: visargaśaktirviśvasya kāraṇaṃ ca nirūpitā aitareyākhyavedānte parameśena vistarāt

plain_english: That which is red is fire; its vigor is sun-and-moon-bodied; thus the letter 'a' is supreme Brahman, whose nature is the arising of that collision.
sanskrit_cite: yallohitaṃ tadagniryadvīryaṃ sūryenduvigraham a iti brahma paramaṃ tatsaṃghaṭṭodayātmakam

plain_english: That seed too has a supreme vital power made of the five elements. As something to be enjoyed it takes the form of food, consisting of sound, touch, and taste.
sanskrit_cite: tasyāpi ca paraṃ vīrya pañcabhūtakalātmakam bhogyatvenānnarūpaṃ ca śabdasparśarasātmakam

plain_english: Sound too is sweet because it increases vital power. That vital power is supreme and pure, and it is understood to have the nature of a desire to emit.
sanskrit_cite: śabdo@pi madhuro yasmādvīryopacayakārakaḥ taddhi vīryaṃ paraṃ śuddhaṃ visisṛkṣātmakaṃ matam

plain_english: That vital power is strength, vigor, the vital breaths, and loveliness. From it offspring arise, and it is also spoken of in ritual acts.

plain_english: In sacrifice and other rites, in rain, in plants, again in vital power, and then in offspring, the same power circulates. Thus emission takes on the form of the whole universe.
sanskrit_cite: yajñādikeṣu tadvṛṣṭau sauṣadhīṣvatha tāḥ punaḥ vīrye tacca prajāsvevaṃ visarge viśvarūpatā

plain_english: That whole mass of sound is called Matrika. Because it enters a state of being both stirred and stirring, it is also declared to be Malini.
sanskrit_cite: śabdarāśiḥ sa evokto mātṛkā sāca kīrtitā kṣobhyakṣobhakatāveśānmālinīṃ tāṃ pracakṣate

plain_english: Malini, beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the rise of emission, is indeed determined to be the supreme power that takes the form of the whole universe.
sanskrit_cite: bījayonisamāpattivisargodayasundarā mālinī hi parā śaktirnirṇītā viśvarūpiṇī

plain_english: In reality this supreme power is one alone and draws forth time. Yet through its connection with the differentiation of the power-holder, it takes on the form of a pair.
sanskrit_cite: eṣā vastuta ekaiva parā kālasya karṣiṇī śaktimadbhedayogena yāmalatvaṃ prapadyate

plain_english: That reflective awareness, whose nature is the perfect I, abides in its own self and, by its freedom, manifests division within itself.
sanskrit_cite: tasya pratyavamarśo yaḥ paripūrṇo@hamātmakaḥ sa svātmani svatantratvādvibhāgamavabhāsayet

plain_english: When division appears, this awareness is said to take a threefold body: Pashyanti, Madhyama, and the gross level called Vaikhari.
sanskrit_cite: vibhāgābhāsane cāsya tridhā vapurudāhṛtam paśyantī madhyamā sthūlā vaikharītyabhiśabditam

plain_english: Each of those three also has a threefold form: gross, subtle, and supreme. Among them is a form beautiful with flowing tones, having the nature of sound.
sanskrit_cite: tāsāmapi tridhā rūpaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ tatra yā svarasandarbhasubhagā nādarūpiṇī

plain_english: That gross aspect is indeed Pashyanti. Since letters and other divisions have not yet appeared there, its single undivided form is called sweetness and power.
sanskrit_cite: sā sthūlā khalu paśyantī varṇādyapravibhāgataḥ avibhāgaikarūpatvaṃ mādhuryaṃ śaktirucyate

plain_english: Clearness and harshness arise from the friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on. Yet in this sound-form they function in close proximity to consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: sthānavāyvādigharṣotthā sphuṭataiva ca pāruṣī tadasyāṃ nādarūpāyāṃ saṃvitsavidhavṛttitaḥ

plain_english: Absorption into that same sound is perceived suddenly. Those who do not become absorbed in it remain sunk in the body and similar limitations.
sanskrit_cite: sājātyāntarma[ttama] yībhūtirjhagityevopalabhyate yeṣāṃ na tanmayībhūtiste dehādinimajjanam

plain_english: Those who do not know remain with their awareness sunk and not centered in the heart. For them, the sound that comes from a skin-covered drum or the like is just an external resonance.
sanskrit_cite: avidanto magnasaṃvinmānāstvahṛdayā iti yattucarmāvanaddhādi kiṃcittatraiṣa yo dhvaniḥ

plain_english: Because it is both clear and unclear, that gross form is Madhyama. Madhyama also contains an undivided aspect, which is described as its coloration.

plain_english: Where sound is made of undivided tones, it is delighting. Non-division brings fulfillment, as can be seen in the recitation of rhythm.
sanskrit_cite: avibhāgasvaramayī yatra syāttatsurañjakam avibhāgo hi nirvṛtyai dṛśyatāṃ tālapāṭhataḥ

plain_english: One feels satisfied in that unmanifest sound during musical playing. Yet that same level can also serve as the cause for the arising of clear letters.
sanskrit_cite: kilāvyaktadhvanau tasminvādane parituṣyati yā tu sphuṭānāṃ varṇānāmutpattau kāraṇaṃ bhavet

sanskrit_cite: pṛthakpṛthaktattritayaṃ sūkṣmamityabhiśabdyate ṣaḍjaṃ karomi madhuraṃ vādayāmi bruve vacaḥ

plain_english: A threefold connecting awareness is indeed experienced separately. Of that triad, the first aspect is a form without limiting condition.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthagevānusandhānatrayaṃ saṃvedyate kila etasyāpi trayasyādyaṃ yadrupamanupādhimat

plain_english: That is the supreme triad. There Shiva is of the nature of supreme consciousness, and in the manifestation of division three principal powers appear.
sanskrit_cite: tatparaṃ tritayaṃ tatra śivaḥ paracidātmakaḥ vibhāgābhāsanāyāṃ ca mukhyāstisro@tra śaktayaḥ

plain_english: The three principal powers are Anuttara as supreme will, the power situated as supreme-and-non-supreme, and the unfolding power called knowledge, which is declared as the lower.
sanskrit_cite: anuttarā parecchā ca parāparatayā sthitā unmeṣaśaktirjñānākhyā tvapareti nigadyate

plain_english: From the stirring of those powers, six immaculate cognitions are declared. They arise from the immersion of those same powers as the power of action.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobharūpātpunastāsāmuktāḥ ṣaṭ saṃvido@malāḥ āsāmeva samāveśātkriyāśaktitayoditāt

plain_english: Twelve cognitions are declared, and in them all is contained. This is the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvido dvādaśa proktā yāsu sarvaṃ samāpyate etāvaddevadevasya mukhyaṃ tacchakticakrakam

plain_english: To this extent, the God of gods, Bhairava, possessed of full power, is of the nature of reflective awareness and is united with emission and projection.
sanskrit_cite: etāvatā devadevaḥ pūrṇaśaktiḥ sa bhairavaḥ parāmarśātmakatvena visargākṣepayogataḥ

plain_english: One should worship the power called the Bhairava-self, surrounded by twelve yoginis; from them the circle of powers extends up to sixty-four.

plain_english: Beginning from the syllable e, it unfolds up to the thousand-spoked; and in the scripture these powers are given many names according to their different functions.
sanskrit_cite: ekārataḥ samārabhya sahasrāraṃ pravartate tāsāṃ ca kṛtyabhedena nāmāni bahudhāgame

plain_english: Their modes of worship, in dual, nondual, and mixed forms, have been explained at great length in the revered Traishira.
sanskrit_cite: upāsāśca dvayādvaitavyāmiśrākārayogataḥ śrīmattraiśirame tacca kathitaṃ vistarādbahu

plain_english: It is not written here, for fear of prolixity and because it is not needed; those same powers are proclaimed as stainless, pure, and not-terrible.
sanskrit_cite: iha no likhitaṃ vyāsabhayāccānupayogataḥ tā eva nirmalāḥ śuddhā aghorāḥ parikīrtitāḥ

plain_english: Because they are the source of the terrible and more terrible forms, they are also of that nature, appearing in creation, maintenance, dissolution, and in the transcendence of those three conditions.
sanskrit_cite: ghoraghoratarāṇāṃ tu sotṛtvācca tadātmikāḥ sṛṣṭau sthitau ca saṃhāre tadupādhitrayātyaye

plain_english: The abiding form of those same powers is divided in many ways, but the teachers say that the form beyond limiting conditions is twofold.
sanskrit_cite: tāsāmeva sthitaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā pravibhajyate upādhyatītaṃ yadrūpaṃ taddvidhā guravo jaguḥ

plain_english: This may be because limiting conditions do not arise, or because they are calmed; and that calming is twofold, either by quieting or by the method of forceful ripening.
sanskrit_cite: anullāsādupādhīnāṃ yadvā praśamayogataḥ praśamaśca dvidhā śāntyā haṭhapākakrameṇa tu

plain_english: The pacification called forceful ripening, fully active through the continual blazing savor of devouring, is the one fit for instruction, because it burns up the fuel of difference.
sanskrit_cite: alaṃ grāsarasākhyena satataṃ jvalanātmanā haṭhapākapraśamanaṃ yattṛtīyaṃ tadeva ca upadeśāya yujyeta bhedendhanavidāhakam

plain_english: When all things are forcefully offered into the fire of one's own awareness, they kindle that fire by their own power and abandon the division of difference.
sanskrit_cite: nijabodhajaṭharahutabhuji bhāvāḥ sarve samarpitā haṭhataḥ vijahati bhedavibhāgaṃ nijaśaktyā taṃ samindhānāḥ

plain_english: When, by forceful ripening, the divided forms of things are dissolved, the goddesses of consciousness consume the whole universe as it becomes nectar.
sanskrit_cite: haṭhapākena bhāvānāṃ rūpe bhinne vilāpite aśnantyamṛtasādbhūtaṃ viśvaṃ saṃvittidevatāḥ

plain_english: Satisfied, they repose without difference upon the god Bhairava, the sky of consciousness, who rests solely in the full heart of their own self.
sanskrit_cite: tāstṛptāḥ svātmanaḥ pūrṇa hṛdayaikāntaśāyinam cidvyomabhairavaṃ devamabhedenādhiśerate

plain_english: Thus, because of their entry into various acts and functions and because of the many names and forms of worship, their manifold form appears even within non-difference.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kṛtyakriyāveśānnāmopāsābahutvataḥ āsāṃ bahuvidhaṃ rūpamabhede@pyavabhāsate

plain_english: And of these very goddesses, through the joining of invocation and dismissal, there is an expansion by groups of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and more.
sanskrit_cite: āsāmeva ca devīnāmāvāpodvāpayogataḥ ekadvitricatuṣpañcaṣaṭsaptāṣṭanavottaraiḥ

plain_english: The extensive division beginning with Rudra, Arka, Anya, Kala, Sena, and so on is vast; enough of further detail—now the discussion turns to the matter at hand.
sanskrit_cite: rudrārkānyakalāsenāprabhṛtirbhedavistaraḥ alamanyena bahunā prakṛte@tha niyujyate

plain_english: This whole expanded group of things shines in the self of consciousness as a reflection; one for whom it appears thus is indeed the Lord of the universe.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvidātmani viśvo@yaṃ bhāvavargaḥ prapañcavān pratibimbatayā bhāti yasya viśveśvaro hi saḥ

plain_english: One in whom such a non-conceptual reflective awareness is ever arising in the self is indeed marked by the Shambhava means.
sanskrit_cite: evamātmani yasyedṛgavikalpaḥ sadodayaḥ parāmarśaḥ sa evāsau śāṃbhavopāyamudritaḥ

plain_english: This is the reflective awareness of full I-ness that has been explained; here there are no other practices such as mantra, mudra, ritual action, or worship.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇāhantāparāmarśo yo@syāyaṃ pravivecitaḥ mantramudrākriyopāsāstadanyā nātra kāścana

plain_english: Resorting again and again to this non-conceptual immersion, one attains the state of Bhairava, also called liberation while living.
sanskrit_cite: bhūyobhūyaḥ samāveśaṃ nirvikalpamimaṃ śritaḥ abhyeti bhairavībhāvaṃ jīvanmuktyaparābhidham

plain_english: From this point onward, liberation while living is examined, where even in brief outline the distinction between means and goal is set forth.
sanskrit_cite: ita eva prabhṛtyeṣā jīvanmuktirvicāryate yatra sūtraṇayāpīyamupāyopeyakalpanā

plain_english: But in the previous chapter there was not even a notion of difference; therefore, in that means-less path, who is liberated, how, or from what?
sanskrit_cite: prāktane tvāhnike kācidbhedasya kalanāpi no tenānupāye tasminko mucyate vā kathaṃ kutaḥ

plain_english: In the non-conceptual reflective awareness called the Shambhava means, the wise person should apply the fiftyfold division that was indicated earlier.
sanskrit_cite: nirvikalpe parāmarśe śāmbhavopāyanāmani pañcāśadbhedatāṃ pūrvasūtritāṃ yojayedbudhaḥ

plain_english: Seeing even the earth itself, without conceptualization, as reflected in one's own self, one attains Bhairava-hood; the same method applies to water and the other elements as well.
sanskrit_cite: dharāmevāvikalpena svātmani pratibimbitām paśyanbhairavatāṃ yāti jalādiṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ

plain_english: At the final limit, one conceives a supreme principle beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, and called Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: yāvadante paraṃ tattvaṃ samastāvaraṇordhvagam vyāpi svatantraṃ sarvajñaṃ yacchivaṃ parikalpitam

plain_english: Seeing even that conceived Shiva reflected in the mirror of unconstructed, noble awareness, and free from conceptual thought, one becomes Bhairava oneself.
sanskrit_cite: tadapyakalpitodārasaṃviddarpaṇabimbitam paśyanvikalpavikalo bhairavībhavati svayam

plain_english: Just as one who sees a red object in front with nonconceptual awareness becomes firmly established in the undivided awareness of that one pot through its various channels.
sanskrit_cite: yathā raktaṃ puraḥ paśyannirvikalpakasaṃvidā tattaddvāraniraṃśaikaghaṭasaṃvittisusthitaḥ

plain_english: In the same way, recognizing one's own self through each and every aggregate beginning with earth, one shines forth as truly full.
sanskrit_cite: tadvaddharādikaikaikasaṃghātasamudāyataḥ parāmṛśansvamātmānaṃ pūrṇa evāvabhāsate

plain_english: This has arisen from me, this is reflected in me alone, and this is not different from me: in this threefold way is the Shambhava means.
sanskrit_cite: matta evoditamidaṃ mayyeva pratibimbitam madabhinnamidaṃ ceti tridhopāyaḥ sa śāmbhavaḥ

plain_english: This is the summary of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal. As it is established and taught, the Spanda teaching states it.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭeḥ sthiteḥ saṃhṛteśca tadetatsūtraṇaṃ kṛtam yatra sthitaṃ yataśceti tadāha spandaśāsane

plain_english: By this alone the supreme sovereign nature of awareness and its identity as the self of all are made known; what other defining mark need be stated?
sanskrit_cite: etāvataiva hyaiśvarya saṃvidaḥ khyāpitaṃ param viśvātmakatvaṃ cetyanyallakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ nu kathyatām

plain_english: In my own self, in the space of consciousness, I manifest the universe; through this expansive recognition as the creator whose self is the universe, Bhairava identity unfolds.
sanskrit_cite: svātmanyeva cidākāśe viśvamasmyavabhāsayan sraṣṭā viśvātmaka iti prathayā bhairavātmatā

plain_english: The entire group of the six paths is reflected in me alone; recognizing 'I am the maker of maintenance' is this clear universal form.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍadhvajātaṃ nikhilaṃ mayyeva pratibimbitam sthitikartāhamasmīti sphuṭeyaṃ viśvarūpatā

plain_english: Seeing that this universe melts in me, in the self matted with the flames of ever-risen great awakening, one becomes still.
sanskrit_cite: sadoditamahābodhajvālājaṭilatātmani viśvaṃ dravati mayyetaditi paśyanpraśāmyati

plain_english: I am Shiva, the exulting fire that burns the dream-house of samsara, filled with endless varied beings.
sanskrit_cite: anantacitrasadgarbhasaṃsārasvapnasadmanaḥ ploṣakaḥ śiva evāhamityullāsī hutāśanaḥ

plain_english: The whole world arises from me in many differentiated forms, yet when it dissolves in me no other remains. One who sees creation, maintenance, and dissolution as play in a partless reality shines forth in the fourth state.
sanskrit_cite: jagatsarvaṃ mattaḥ prabhavati vibhedena bahudhā tathāpyetadrūḍhaṃ mayi vigalite tvatra na paraḥ taditthaṃ yaḥ sṛṣṭisthitivilayabhekīkṛtivaśādanaṃśaṃ paśyetsa sphurati hi turīyaṃ padabhitaḥ

plain_english: In that supreme means, abounding in Shaiva non-duality, some indeed attain trust, being cultivated by the lord of bound souls.
sanskrit_cite: tadasminparamopāye śāmbhavādvaitaśālini ke@pyeva yānti viśvāsaṃ pasmeśena bhāvitāḥ

plain_english: Bathing, vow, body purification, retention, mantra application, path arrangement, sacrifice rite, offering, recitation, and concentration.
sanskrit_cite: snānaṃ vrataṃ dehaśuddhirdhāraṇā mantrayojanā adhvaklṛptiryāgavidhirhomajapyasamādhayaḥ

plain_english: Such imaginings are not fitted here by difference; the grace-causing state of one present here is clearly established.
sanskrit_cite: ityādikalpanā kāpi nātra bhedena yujyate parānugrahakāritvamatrasthasya sphuṭaṃ sthitam

plain_english: If one worthy of such grace approaches the teacher, then he is such; he would not be through devotion to becoming, but cultivated.
sanskrit_cite: yadi tādṛganugrāhyo daiśikasyopasarpati athāsau tādṛśo na syādbhavabhaktyā ca bhāvitaḥ

plain_english: He worships him; then, from the cultivated grace-giver, he should learn the various initiation rites.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ cārādhayate bhāvitādṛśānugraheritaḥ tadā vicitraṃ dīkṣādividhiṃ śikṣeta koviṃdaḥ

plain_english: Future ones too have those devotions; they attain completion, and this essence-state, supreme and to be obtained, is described as Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvinyo@pi hyupāsāstā straivāyānti niṣṭhitim etanmayatvaṃ paramaṃ prāpyaṃ nirvarṇyateśivam

plain_english: Thus this supreme Shaiva self-knowledge has been told in great detail.
